title: CIP dissector: Improve STRINGI support
description:
* Fix issue where parsed length of STRINGI entries was incorrect
* Add support for STRINGN data type
* Display string data type in the tree
* Display character set in the tree
* Make each STRINGI block its own subtree with a name
* Improve filtering and readability options

AI-Assisted: no

Use \_U\_ in the argument list for an unused parameter
This switch statement could also handle the "unsupported" bytes per character and just return
I’m not sure I understand what’s being requested.

changed this line in [version 6 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/24051/diffs?diff_id=1720188151&start_sha=bc68eb8fc322fa9db647e5153c449aa3706d52a3#20e5a2e6b1cee42c82daa2eea183b8ea79c64c5d_6598_6588)
If there is a "too short" STRINGI, wouldn't you like Wireshark to catch it with a malformed packet instead of silently ignoring it? (which would happen if you remove the tvb_bytes_exist().
You mean calling expert_add_info_format or similar before returning?

Potentially, yes.  To me there are 3 options:
1. Silently fail and leave bytes undissected (current implementation, not advised)
2. Add expert information showing device/developer error and leave partial STRINGI entry undissected, but at least the expert information is filterable (if checking for conformance)
3. Don't have a size check at all and let proto_tree_add_xxx throw an exception at the exact field that caused the overrun.

I have always struggled with picking between 2 and 3 (in general for any protocol) as the target audience here is EtherNet/IP (stack) developers and the choice rarely matters "in the real world". And as a developer, I think I prefer number 3.  Wireshark just doesn't like to see bytes go undissected.
Three. Mainly because it's _they_ common way to signal that the underlying SDU is cut short, independent of protocol.
